sections.what_happened: [ATTRIBUTED REPORT] Brent crude slipped toward ~$114 on Thu Oct 29 after settling Oct 28 at $113.88 (-$1.93, -1.67%); WTI settled $99.90 (-1.83%) and traded below $102 on Oct 29. JPMorgan's model puts Brent fair value at $94, leaving a ~$20 war premium attributed to geopolitical risk around Hormuz; the bank finds no evidence freight costs explain the gap. Crude delivered to Asia averaged $131/barrel in October (JPMorgan estimate). BMI (Fitch Solutions unit) expects a preliminary Hormuz deal likeliest in early 2027, Brent averaging $107 this quarter and $112 in Q1 2027, then $67 by Q4 2027 if a deal lands -- a forecast, not a fact. US EIA: crude inventories fell 1.9M barrels last week to lowest since July; exports at strongest pace since May. European gas futures jumped >5% above EUR 100/MWh, first time since Dec 2022. Brent is up >17% in October (NDTV Profit/Trading Economics).

JPMorgan $20-premium figure reaches this scan only via an UNDECLARED carrier (CryptoRank/BeInCrypto) and therefore does not add a declared family; the Oct 28 settlement figure is a Reuters Houston piece via an undeclared carry (balitangmarino). Per the sig>=3 gate scope, a sig-2 item is not held on the single-family ground alone, but the JPMorgan figure must be carried as attributed-via-carry, not as a directly retrieved bank report.
sections.what_disputed: Brent direction is contested intraday: Oct 28 settled DOWN ~$2 on diplomatic headlines while Oct 29 morning pieces describe a pullback from four-year highs -- the premium story and the dip story are both true at different timestamps; do not present $114 as a spike. BMI's $67 Q4-2027 figure is a conditional forecast. PortWatch backbone: NO new snapshot; latest remains Oct 26 fetch / Oct 18 observation (STALE: Hormuz 4 transits, 7-day avg 3.7 vs 2025 baseline 85.5/day) -- no counted transit figure is cited as current here, and the $20 premium must not be presented as a counted-flow fact.
